chapter_seo_title: Daoist Who Exorcises and Keeps the Ghost—509 Explained
chapter_meta_description: The Lü Family Troupe stumbles onto a false exorcism by a cunning Daoist. A copper-coin sword link ties this side story back to Li Huowang’s present.
og_title: Exorcist or Ghost-Keeper? Chapter 509 of Dao Gui Yi Xian
og_description: Follow the Lü Family Troupe through a tense, back-alley exorcism that twists into a bigger peril.
twitter_description: A shady Daoist’s fake exorcism reveals a connection to Li Huowang.

lore_anchors.definition: A Daoist ritual weapon made from coins strung on red cord, used for exorcism and spirit-binding. In this chapter, its reappearance signals a link to Li Huowang.
A title for Daoist priests who claim authority to command spirits and perform high-level exorcisms; often used as a rhetorical flourish by itinerant sorcerers.
A small statue of a bodhisattva seated backward, considered an unlucky or heretical devotional object in some folk traditions; here used as a vessel for the black smoke entity.
Refers to a tongue from a person with the Heart-Element constitution, a rare and valuable alchemical ingredient; the Daoist’s final discovery is a double windfall.
An amulet or talisman carved from decayed wood, used by Gouwa as a defensive implement; it is effective against the animated black gown.
In Chinese folk culture, gong beats are used to alert people to red (joyous) or white (funeral) events; for performers, they indicate potential work.
